Recommendation: Decommission or replace all EOL assets
Description: Migrate Linux Kernel 2.6 (179.61.230.146) to AlmaLinux 9 or RHEL 9. Migrate CentOS 7 hosts (200.31.177.194, 201.190.14.22) to AlmaLinux 9, Rocky Linux 9, or RHEL 9. Contact Dell for Wyse ThinOS firmware upgrade options. After migration, deploy jQuery v3.7.x updates on all migrated hosts.
Vulnerabilities_Addressed: 5 Critical (EOL Reclassified) - jQuery XSS on EOL hosts

Recommendation: Disable SSLv2 and SSLv3 on Fortinet FortiGate
Description: Navigate to the SSL/TLS profile for the HTTPS administrative interface and any SSL-VPN configurations on FortiGate 190.143.139.250. Set minimum TLS version to TLS 1.2 (config vpn ssl settings / set algorithm high). Validate via rescan — SSL Version 2 and 3 Protocol Detection plugin must return no findings.
Vulnerabilities_Addressed: 1 Critical - SSL Version 2 and 3 Protocol Detection

Recommendation: Upgrade jQuery to v3.7.x across all affected web servers
Description: Replace legacy jQuery 1.x/2.x includes with jQuery v3.7.1 on all affected web servers. For Cisco appliance and Wyse ThinOS web UIs apply the latest vendor firmware which bundles updated jQuery. Confirm remediation via Nessus plugin 145023 rescan. On EOL hosts this must accompany not replace the OS migration in Recommendation 1.
Operating_System: Linux Kernel 2.6 (EOL), Linux Kernel 4.x AlmaLinux, CentOS 7 (EOL)
Vulnerabilities_Addressed: 9 - jQuery XSS instances (5 Critical EOL Reclassified + 4 Medium)

Description: Establish and enforce patching cadence using Tenable.io SLA tracking: Critical <= 30 days, High <= 60 days, Medium <= 90 days. Assign each finding to an ITSM ticket at scan completion. Generate weekly aging reports distributed to regional IT leads and the CISO. 100% of current findings exceed the 90-day SLA threshold.
Vulnerabilities_Addressed: 30 - All C/H/M findings (100% aged beyond SLA)

Recommendation: Remediate SWEET32 on FortiGate with comprehensive cipher hardening
Description: Disable all 3DES/TDEA cipher suites on FortiGate 190.143.139.250. Configure SSL/TLS profiles to permit only ECDHE and DHE cipher suites with AES-128-GCM or AES-256-GCM (AEAD ciphers). Coordinate all FortiGate cipher changes (SSLv2/v3, RC4, 3DES, TLS 1.0) in a single maintenance window to minimize operational impact.
Vulnerabilities_Addressed: 1 High - SSL Medium Strength Cipher Suites (SWEET32) on FortiGate

Recommendation: Enforce TLS 1.2 minimum on F5 BIG-IP and Microsoft Windows
Description: On F5 BIG-IP 200.114.112.164: update the Client SSL profile under LTM > Profiles > SSL > Client SSL and set Minimum Version to TLSv1.2. On Windows 45.191.246.102: apply SCHANNEL registry keys to disable TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 or deploy via Group Policy Object targeting SSL Cipher Suite Order. Also eliminates SWEET32 findings on ports 443, 3400 and 4446.

Recommendation: Replace self-signed and untrusted SSL certificates with CA-issued certificates
Description: On FortiGate: replace default self-signed cert under System > Certificates > Local Certificates. On F5 BIG-IP: update SSL profile to reference CA-issued cert under LTM > Profiles > SSL. On Windows: replace certificate in IIS or the applicable application service. Ensure all CSRs specify SHA-256 as the signature algorithm — this simultaneously resolves MD5/SHA-1 findings (Recommendation 9).
Operating_System: FortiOS on Fortinet FortiGate, F5 Networks BIG-IP, Microsoft Windows
Vulnerabilities_Addressed: 6 - SSL Certificate Cannot Be Trusted (x4) + SSL Self-Signed Certificate (x2)

Recommendation: Disable RC4 cipher suites (Bar Mitzvah) on FortiGate and Microsoft Windows
Description: FortiGate 190.143.139.250: remove RC4 variants from SSL/TLS cipher list in the profile configuration. Windows 45.191.246.102: set Enabled=0 under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Ciphers\RC4 128/128 or apply CIS Benchmark Level 1 hardening GPO which includes RC4 disablement.
Operating_System: FortiOS on Fortinet FortiGate, Microsoft Windows
Vulnerabilities_Addressed: 2 - SSL RC4 Cipher Suites Supported (Bar Mitzvah)

Recommendation: Replace MD5/SHA-1 signed certificates with SHA-256 or stronger
Description: Replace any certificates signed with MD5 or SHA-1 with new certificates using SHA-256 or stronger signing algorithms. This action is best coordinated with Recommendation 7 — when obtaining new CA-issued certificates ensure the Certificate Signing Request (CSR) specifies SHA-256 as the signature algorithm. Verify using: openssl s_client -connect host:port | openssl x509 -noout -text confirming sha256WithRSAEncryption.
Operating_System: FortiOS on Fortinet FortiGate, Microsoft Windows
Vulnerabilities_Addressed: 2 - SSL Certificate Signed Using Weak Hashing Algorithm
